//: Story Phase 3 crew dialogue by stage: s9 evening (before the declaration), s10a declared, s10b renamed, s11 night (Frog Grog), s12 morning (the ship changing), s13 sharks, s14 after the lure, end (after the phase).
hale.p3_s9: hale[resigned]: Evening, Captain. The crew are... improvising.
hale: Rook has a sock on his face. Bob is breathing through a bottle. Sully has put candle wax somewhere I shan't describe.
hale[concerned]: And Garrick is standing on a barrel in a curtain. I thought you should know before you saw it.
hale.p3_s10a: hale[concerned]: 'Grand Stenchmaster of the Seven Seas.'
hale: He's had it painted on a plank, sir. Quill says the paint's his.
hale[resigned]: I've served under pirates who called themselves admirals. At least they had a ship.
hale.p3_s10b: hale: Forgive me, sir. It's in the air. Everything is in the air.
hale.p3_s11: hale[resigned]: Rain on top of it. I didn't think it could get worse. It found a way.
hale.p3_s12: hale[concerned]: The ship's behaving oddly, Captain. I don't know how else to put it.
hale: The sails breathe. The bell coughs. The ropes are... damp.
hale[resigned]: I've a list. The list has a smell.
hale.p3_s13: hale[alarmed]: I'll say it, Captain. I didn't believe him about the sharks.
hale: I believe him now. I believe him completely.
hale.p3_s14: hale: He came back, sir. I'll confess I hadn't counted on that.
hale[resigned]: And the sharks went where he went. I've no idea what to do with that information.
hale.p3_end: hale: All hands know the drill now, Captain Stinkbeard. Stomach noise, rowboat, downwind.
hale[resigned]: I heard myself say 'Grand Stenchmaster' in the log this morning without laughing. I think something in me has died.
quill.p3_s9: quill[disgusted]: I've tied a scented handkerchief to my quill. I can't smell it. I can only smell him.
quill: Garrick asked me for a ledger. A good one. Leather-bound. I gave him the worst one we had.
quill.p3_s10a: quill[concerned]: He asked what the Grand Stenchmaster's salary should be entered as.
quill: I wrote 'nothing'. He crossed it out and wrote 'executive'.
quill[annoyed]: That's not a number, I told him. He said, 'Not yet.'
quill.p3_s10b: quill: I'll need to amend the manifest, Captain. Under 'master'.
quill[concerned]: I'll write... 'Captain S.' Discreetly. Nobody reads the manifest.
quill: Except the Navy. And the harbourmasters. And... everybody.
quill.p3_s11: quill[devastated]: The grog, Captain. Forty-one barrels on my books. I can smell every one of them from here.
quill: I used to be able to tell rum from brandy by the bouquet. Now it's all the same bouquet.
quill.p3_s12: quill: I've started a column for 'smells, new'. It's the longest column in the ledger.
quill.p3_s13: quill[alarmed]: Captain, the sharks are eating the parts of the ship I've already paid for!
quill.p3_s14: quill: Damage: one hull plank, one rudder, one barrel of Frog Grog, one oar.
quill[concerned]: And one small shark, returned to the sea. Undamaged. I checked.
quill.p3_end: quill: The Grand Stenchmaster's expenses are under 'Emergencies, Digestive'. I've had to open a new page.
mags.p3_s9: mags[disgusted]: I can't cook, Captain. Everything I make tastes of the air, and the air tastes of him.
mags: I've started knitting instead. Squawks needs a second jumper. Maybe a third. Maybe a whole wardrobe.
mags.p3_s10a: mags[angry]: 'Grand Stenchmaster'! I'll give him a grand something. With a ladle.
mags.p3_s10b: mags[laugh]: It's... it's got a ring to it, Captain. Sorry. Sorry. It's the fumes.
mags.p3_s11: mags[disgusted]: I tried a drop from every barrel in the stores. For science.
mags: The one by the stove is least terrible. It's still terrible. But least.
mags.p3_s12: mags: Jim's fish came up smoked. I'm not touching it. Neither should you, Captain.
mags.p3_s13: mags[alarmed]: Sharks! Sharks in the soup! Not IN the soup. Near the soup. Near the ship. Where's the soup?
mags.p3_s14: mags[annoyed]: He ate my whole pot of beans, you know. In a rowboat. With sharks.
mags: Didn't even leave the pot. Well. He left it at the bottom of the sea.
mags.p3_end: mags: I've put a pot of beans by the rowboat. Permanent. For emergencies.
mags[disgusted]: I never thought I'd say that about a pot of beans.
fennimore.p3_s9: fennimore[concerned]: Squawks has no fever, Captain. Just no feathers. And a great deal of opinion.
fennimore: Keep him warm and keep him away from Garrick. For both their sakes.
fennimore.p3_s10a: fennimore: A title like that usually comes with a diagnosis. I'm still working on his.
fennimore.p3_s10b: fennimore[smug]: Clinically speaking, Captain, the name is accurate.
fennimore: I say that as your doctor. And as a man standing upwind.
fennimore.p3_s11: fennimore[disgusted]: My medicinal brandy, Captain. For wounds and nerves.
fennimore: I'd sooner put the wound in the brandy than the brandy in the wound now.
fennimore.p3_s12: fennimore: I've prescribed Frog Grog for three men with fume cough. It works. I hate that it works.
fennimore.p3_s13: fennimore[alarmed]: Keep your hands inside the rail, Captain! I can stitch a lot of things. I can't stitch a shark back out.
fennimore.p3_s14: fennimore: I checked Garrick over. Bite marks on his coat, his hat, his boots and his oar.
fennimore[smug]: Not one on Garrick. I think the sharks know better.
fennimore.p3_end: fennimore: Squawks's new feather is healthy, Captain. Strong quill. Very, ah... distinctive colour.
fennimore[smug]: Golden, of course. As you said.
brask.p3_s9: brask[disgusted]: I've stood next to a powder magazine going up, Captain. It smelled better than this.
brask.p3_s10a: brask[annoyed]: Grand Stenchmaster. I'll grand him out of the number two gun if he stands near it.
brask.p3_s11: brask[disgusted]: Grog's gone, Captain. The powder's still dry. That's the only good news I've got.
brask.p3_s12: brask: The guns are fine, Captain. Ask me after I fire one.
brask.p3_cannons: brask[disgusted]: Captain. Come and look at this.
A thin yellow wisp is curling out of the mouth of the number three gun. Nobody has fired it.
brask: She coughed at me. Garrick says they'll all do it once they've 'soaked'.
brask[annoyed]: Yellow smoke, Captain. Out of MY guns. The enemy'll think we're firing custard.
captain: Will it do any harm?
brask: To them? Garrick says morale damage 'considerable'.
brask.p3_s13: brask[alarmed]: Can't shoot a shark, Captain! Too low, too fast, and they'd only come back with friends!
brask.p3_s14: brask: I'll give him this. He drew them off better than a broadside would.
brask[annoyed]: Don't tell him I said so.
brask.p3_end: brask: The number three gun coughs on the hour now. Same time as the bell.
nell.p3_s9: nell[disgusted]: She still answers the helm, Captain. She's just... reluctant about it.
nell: Like she's embarrassed to be seen.
nell.p3_s10a: nell: Grand Stenchmaster. I'm writing it in the log exactly as he spelled it. With the extra H.
nell.p3_s10b: nell: Aye aye, Captain St— Captain.
nell[smug]: Heading's steady, sir. Whatever we call you.
nell.p3_s11: nell: Rain, Captain. Warm rain. Somehow it smells too.
nell[disgusted]: I've been at the helm three hours. My nose gave up in the first ten minutes. My eyes are still fighting.
nell.p3_s12: nell: The heading's good. The chart's the problem.
nell.p3_chart: A yellow blot has crept across the chart, spreading from exactly where the wreck-waters are marked.
ned[determined]: It's impossible. A chart can't smell worse the closer you get to somewhere.
nell: I moved the dividers across it. It gets worse near the wreck-waters. I checked twice.
ned[disgusted]: I checked three times. Still impossible.
garrick: Maps absorb the destination, Captain. Everyone knows that.
nell.p3_s13: nell[alarmed]: Something's at the rudder, Captain! She's fighting me!
nell.p3_s14: nell: Rudder's cracked, but she answers. I'll baby her.
nell[smug]: I've steered worse. Not much worse.
nell.p3_end: nell: Sails puff out by themselves now, Captain. A knot, maybe a knot and a half. Free.
nell[disgusted]: I will never, ever put that in the log.
wick.p3_s9: wick[queasy]: Doc says a wet cloth helps, Captain. It does. For about a minute.
wick: Then it's just a wet cloth that smells.
wick.p3_notice: wick[alarmed]: The mainmast, Captain! The notice! It's nailed on the side facing the hatch.
wick[concerned]: I only read the first line. I didn't want to read the second line.
wick.p3_s10a: wick[concerned]: Does he get a hat? If he's a Grand Something he'll want a hat.
wick: Oh. He's got the pot.
wick.p3_s10b: wick[surprised]: I didn't say it! I was going to say 'Captain, Sir'! 'Sti' is short for 'Sir'!
wick[concerned]: It's short for 'Sir' in some places.
wick.p3_s11: wick[queasy]: I had one sip of the grog. Just to see.
wick.p3_s12: wick: The hammocks sigh now, Captain. When you lie down. Like they're tired of us.
wick[concerned]: Jory's looking into it. Jory looks scared.
wick.p3_s13: wick[alarmed]: Captain, one of them looked at me! Right at me! With its face!
wick.p3_s14: wick: I've been thinking about the drinking water, Captain.
wick[concerned]: I've decided not to think about it anymore.
wick.p3_end: wick[happy]: I've made a sign for the rowboat, Captain. It says 'STENCHMASTER'S OFFICE'. He hasn't seen it yet.
rook.p3_s9: rook[queasy]: Wet sock, Captain. Clean one. Well. Cleanish.
rook: Helps with the smell. Doesn't help with the other smell. The sock smell.
rook.p3_s10a: rook[annoyed]: Seven seas. He's never sailed one. He floated in on a bathtub.
rook.p3_s10b: rook[surprised]: That just came out, Captain. I'm sorry. I'm putting the sock back on.
rook.p3_s11: rook[queasy]: Tastes like hot onions and old trousers, Captain.
rook: And I've tasted old trousers. Long story. A shipwreck.
rook.p3_s12: rook: The mainsail breathed at me this morning, Captain. In. Out. No wind.
rook[queasy]: I've stopped standing under it.
rook.p3_s13: rook[alarmed]: Captain, there's one down there with a notch in its fin. It's been round three times. I think it knows my face.
rook.p3_s14: rook: I got the little one off his rowboat with a boathook. It didn't want to let go.
rook.p3_end: rook: Frog Grog's all right if you drink it fast.
rook[queasy]: And don't breathe. And don't swallow.
sully.p3_s9: sully[queasy]: Wax up the nose, Captain. Candle wax.
sully: Works a treat. Can't smell a thing. Can't breathe either, mind. Swings and roundabouts.
sully.p3_s10a: sully[annoyed]: He says the Grand Stenchmaster 'declares evacuation zones'.
sully: I said every room on this ship's an evacuation zone. He said, 'Then that's a good day's work done.'
sully.p3_s10b: sully[happy]: Just practising, Captain! In case it catches on.
captain[angry]: It is NOT catching on.
sully: Right. Right you are. Captain.
sully.p3_s11: sully[queasy]: The garlic comes back, Captain. After. The garlic comes back as more garlic.
sully.p3_s12: sully: Can't scrub it out, Captain. The yellow. It's in the grain.
sully[sad]: I'll keep trying. It's all I know.
sully.p3_s13: sully[alarmed]: They're biting the stained bits, Captain! The bits I couldn't scrub! I KNEW I should've scrubbed harder!
sully.p3_s14: sully: Grand Stenchmaster. Suppose it's earned a bit, now.
sully[annoyed]: A bit. A small bit.
sully.p3_end: sully: Scrubbing duty's easy now, Captain. The stains don't come out, so you're done as soon as you start.
sully[happy]: Best job on the ship.
finch.p3_s9: finch: Sixty years at sea, Captain. I've smelled a whale that died in the sun.
finch[disgusted]: I'd go back to the whale.
finch.p3_s10a: finch: In my day we had one title aboard a ship. 'Captain'. And one for the rest of us. 'Hey, you.'
finch.p3_s10b: finch: Knew a Captain Rottentooth once. Fine seaman. Everybody forgot the name was an insult after a year.
finch[happy]: Took him two years to forgive 'em, mind.
finch.p3_s11: finch[sad]: My bottle, Captain. My secret bottle. Forty years hidden in that locker.
finch: Now it's Frog. Everything's Frog.
finch.p3_s12: finch: The bell's got a cough. I've had that cough. Chew some ginger, I told it.
finch.p3_s13: finch[alarmed]: Sharks! Keep your elbows in, lads! They go for elbows!
finch: They don't, actually. But keep 'em in.
finch.p3_s14: finch: Drew them off with his own stink, Captain. I've seen whalers use blood.
finch.p3_end: finch: 'Grand Stenchmaster'. I've started saying it without thinking.
finch[sad]: That's how they get you.
jory.p3_s9: jory[disgusted]: I've been all over the hold with a lantern, Captain. There's no leak I can plug for this.
jory: The smell's IN the wood now. You can't caulk a smell.
jory.p3_s10a: jory[annoyed]: He wants me to build him a 'proper office'. With a door that locks from the inside.
jory: I said a ship already has one of those. It's called the brig.
jory.p3_s10b: jory: Captain... Stinkbeard. Captain. I'll pick one when you pick one.
jory.p3_s11: jory: I've tasted worse, Captain. Not on purpose.
jory.p3_hammocks: jory[determined]: Captain. Watch the hammock. The empty one.
Nothing happens. Then, very slowly, the empty hammock sags and lets out a long, faint, yellow sigh.
jory[alarmed]: It does that when it warms up! Garrick says body heat 'reactivates' it!
jory: Nobody's slept in it since.
jory[determined]: I'm going to take it down, and I'm going to burn it, and I'm going to sleep on the deck.
jory.p3_s12: jory: I'm not going near the hammocks again till someone tells me they've stopped.
jory.p3_s13: jory[alarmed]: Planks, Captain! Every time they bite we lose a plank!
jory.p3_s14: jory: Patch is holding, Captain. Rudder's cracked, not broken. I'll strap it tonight.
jory.p3_end: jory: I've built the Grand Stenchmaster a bench in the rowboat. Padded.
jory[annoyed]: The sooner he's comfortable out there, the longer he'll stay out there.
bob.p3_s9: bob[queasy]: I'm breathing through a bottle, Captain. An empty one.
bob[happy]: Mostly empty. It had lamp oil in it. That's a nice smell by comparison.
bob.p3_s10a: bob[surprised]: Does the Grand Stenchmaster get paid, Captain?
bob.p3_s10b: bob[happy]: I like it, Captain. Stinkbeard. It's friendly. It sounds like somebody's uncle.
bob.p3_s11: bob[happy]: I LIKE the grog, Captain.
bob: Everyone's looking at me. Should I not like the grog?
bob.p3_s12: bob: I licked the rope, Captain.
bob.p3_s13: bob[alarmed]: I tried to scare one off with my bottle mask, Captain. It scared ME off.
bob.p3_s14: bob[happy]: Frog Water! I'd drink Frog Water.
bob: Nobody'll let me near the water barrel now.
bob.p3_end: bob[happy]: Frog Grog, Captain! Least terrible barrel's the one with the frog painted on.
bob: All of them have the frog painted on. But that one most.
ned.p3_s9: ned[disgusted]: Clear night, Captain. Clear air. Somewhere. Not here.
ned.p3_s10a: ned[determined]: I've been lookout eighteen years. I've never seen a Grand Stenchmaster.
ned: I've still never seen one. That's a man in a curtain.
ned.p3_s10b: ned: Sail ho, Captain Stink— Captain.
ned[surprised]: There's no sail. I just wanted to see if I could say it. I can't.
ned.p3_s11: ned: Can't see past the bow in this rain, Captain. Just as well. Nothing out there wants to see us either.
ned.p3_s12: ned[determined]: Charts don't smell. I'll die on this hill, Captain.
ned.p3_s13: ned[alarmed]: Fins to port! Fins to starboard! Fins... fins everywhere, Captain! I'm running out of directions!
ned.p3_s14: ned: Still a few fins out there, Captain. Hanging back. Waiting, maybe.
ned[concerned]: I don't like it when they wait.
ned.p3_end: ned: I keep one eye on the horizon and one eye on the rowboat, Captain.
ned[determined]: Only got the one eye. It's a busy job.
jim.p3_s9: jim[annoyed]: I pickle things, Captain. I've pickled things for thirty years.
jim[disgusted]: I've never once made the air itself sour. That takes a special talent.
jim.p3_s10a: jim[annoyed]: If he's Grand Stenchmaster, what does that make the cook? Minor Stenchmaster?
jim: I've been stinking up this galley honestly for years. I want credit.
jim.p3_s10b: jim: Stinkbeard, is it. Well, Captain.
jim[annoyed]: At least yours is only a name. Mine's the whole galley.
jim.p3_s11: jim[disgusted]: Even the cooking brandy, Captain. I could flambé with it. Wouldn't dare. It might flambé back.
jim.p3_fish: jim[happy]: Captain! Look at this. Came straight up off the line.
Salty Jim holds up a fish. It is brown, stiff and faintly steaming.
jim: Smoked! Already smoked! Garrick said they would be, near the ship. Saves me hours!
jim: Of course it tastes like the ship. It's been swimming in the ship.
jim[sad]: No advantage, Captain. No advantage at all.
jim.p3_s12: jim: I'm throwing every fish back. They come up smoked. They taste of us.
jim.p3_s13: jim[alarmed]: They followed the fish scraps once, Captain. Now they're following the SHIP.
jim.p3_s14: jim: Gave him my best beans, Captain. Soaked, spiced, a clove of garlic for every one.
jim[sad]: God forgive me. It worked.
jim.p3_end: jim: New rule in my galley, Captain. Nothing goes to the Grand Stenchmaster without a note to the captain first.
penhallow.p3_s9: penhallow[disgusted]: I was ransomed once, you know. By a man who smelled of fish.
penhallow[offended]: I would give anything to be ransomed by him again.
penhallow.p3_s10a: penhallow[smug]: A title bestowed by oneself is worth exactly what one paid for it.
penhallow: I'm a cloth merchant. I know what a curtain costs. Not much.
penhallow.p3_s10b: penhallow[smug]: 'Stinkbeard'. When I'm ransomed, I'll tell everyone in port.
penhallow[terrified]: ...I will not tell anyone in port.
penhallow.p3_s11: penhallow[disgusted]: They offered me a mug. For the toast.
penhallow: I told them I'm a prisoner, not a volunteer.
penhallow.p3_s12: penhallow[offended]: My chains are damp. Why are my chains damp?
penhallow.p3_s13: penhallow[terrified]: Is the ship sinking? Tell me if the ship is sinking. I'm chained to it.
penhallow.p3_s14: penhallow: I've seen merchants drive off pirates with cannon. With bribes. With lies.
penhallow[disgusted]: I have never seen one drive off sharks with... that.
penhallow.p3_end: penhallow: My ransom price keeps falling, Captain. Nobody wants me back smelling like this.
dunstan.p3_s9: dunstan: Tried to sleep through it, Captain. Can't. I dream in yellow now.
dunstan.p3_s10a: dunstan: Grand what? I was asleep.
dunstan.p3_s10b: dunstan: Captain Stink— sorry, sir. Half asleep. The name was in my dream too.
dunstan.p3_s11: dunstan: Grog's gone, sir? I'll go back to sleep, then. Nothing to stay up for.
dunstan.p3_s12: dunstan: My hammock sighed at me. I'm sleeping standing up now. Like a horse.
dunstan.p3_s13: dunstan: Sharks, sir? I'll stay below. I've heard sharks don't come below.
dunstan.p3_s14: dunstan: Is it safe to sleep again, sir? It's never safe to sleep again, is it.
dunstan.p3_end: dunstan: Middle watch is quieter now, sir. Just the bell coughing and a rowboat laughing, far off.
gristle.p3_breath: Gristle, the ship's rigger, is holding his breath. His face is the colour of a boiled crab.
captain: Gristle. You can't hold it forever.
gristle[disgusted]: Oh no. Oh, that was worse. It's worse when it comes in all at once.
gristle: Three minutes, Captain. Three minutes I held it. And it was waiting for me the whole time.
gristle.p3_s10a: gristle[annoyed]: Grand Stenchmaster. I've spliced ropes longer than his career.
gristle.p3_s10b: gristle: I won't call you it, Captain.
gristle[smug]: I'll think it very loudly, but I won't call you it.
gristle.p3_s11: gristle: Rigging's wet through, Captain. And not from the rain. I'll say no more.
gristle.p3_s12: gristle[disgusted]: Don't grab the lines bare-handed, Captain. Trust me.
gristle.p3_s13: gristle[alarmed]: They've had a go at the rudder lines, Captain! Chewed 'em like liquorice!
gristle.p3_s14: gristle: I held my breath the whole time he was being lowered. Thought it best.
gristle[queasy]: Still regretting the bit after.
gristle.p3_end_1: gristle: Suspicious gurgle drill, Captain. I'm fastest to the rowboat on this ship. Eight seconds.
gristle[smug]: The Grand Stenchmaster took eleven. Carrying beans.
gristle.p3_end_2: gristle: The ropes still sweat, Captain. I've made my peace with it.
gristle[queasy]: I haven't made my peace with it.
